title: Blessed
text:
Blessed be you, because you made me

love death, which before I feared.

Since you went away from my side,

I love death when I am sad;

if I am joyful, still more.


In other times, its glacial scythe

gave me terrors; today, it is a friend.

And I sense it so maternal!...

You performed such a prodigy.

God bless you! God bless you!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the paradox of bereavement making death maternal.

title: Perhaps
text:
Perhaps my moan no longer matters to her

in the indifferent silent Eden

where the disembodied spirit

lives as if asleep...

Perhaps she no longer even knows how I have wept

nor how I have suffered.


In deep quietism,

her soul, which once loved me so,

slides glacially through that abyss

of eternal muteness,

forgetful of itself, of me, of everything...
editorial_note: The translation preserves the cold distance of the disembodied beloved.

title: Lord, You Watered the Fields with Flowers...
text:
Lord, You watered the fields with flowers

that fill the air with aroma and freshness,

you covered the heavens with immense splendors

and gave the seas their eternal murmur.


Everywhere your matchless love shines;

the earth proclaims your glory everywhere;

and amid those hymns that spring from the world,

I want to raise to you my voice of pleasure.
editorial_note: This first-line version preserves the same devotional offering of voice and praise.

title: Madrigal
editorial_note: The translation keeps the double movement of being lost and saved by the same green eyes.

title: For Your Green Eyes I Would Lose Myself...
editorial_note: This related version keeps the repeated green eyes and the final saving spell.

title: On Finding Some Flasks of Essence
text:
Even her perfumes last longer than she!

See here the flasks, which she scarcely used,

and which reconstruct for me the subtle

trace she left in the house...


Hermetically enclosed,

the essence in its bottles will not escape.

While the spirit of my dearly beloved,

more imponderable, more tenuous perhaps,

flew from her lips, enchanted retort,

and where can it be!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the contrast between lasting perfume and vanished spirit.

title: Identity
text:
Whoever knows he is one with God attains Nirvana:

a Nirvana in which every darkness is illumined;

vertiginous widening of human consciousness,

which is only a projection of the Divine Idea

in Time...


The phenomenon, the exterior, vain fruit

of illusion, is extinguished: there is no longer plurality,

and the I, ecstatic, at last plunges into the absolute,

and has all eternity as inheritance!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the metaphysical arc from illusion to absolute identity.
